items.title: How are we all feeling about AI right now? – Deseret News
items.summary: Fast-emerging artificial intelligence tools and software are stoking plenty of concerns as an increasing number of AI-driven misdeeds are reported. And alongside those incidents, predictions are coming from some within the AI development world that the technology could advance to the point of threatening the whole of humanity. [...] Johns Hopkins University professor and AI researcher Christopher Honey reviewed the new polling data and, in a Deseret News interview, said he sees a notable convergence between the Deseret News poll’s findings on artificial intelligence and what he discovered in his own national polling — people want safeguards around AI, but they also hope the technology will deliver meaningful advances. [...] Faster medical research and new treatments; earlier, more accurate diagnosis of disease; and scientific discovery beyond health occupied the top spots for both polling samples. Both audiences also matched up in their next three AI hopefulness rankings of improving accessibility for people with disabilities; lowering the cost of goods and services; and taking over dangerous or repetitive work.

items.summary:
Chiến thắng áp đảo của đảng Dn chủ trong cuộc bầu cử giữa kỳ của Mỹ đã làm dấy lên lo ngại về triển vọng của ngành trí tuệ nhn tạo và bán dẫn. Điều này khiến cổ phiếu công nghệ cao của Mỹ biến động.  
   
Đảng Dn chủ đã giành lại quyền kiểm soát cả hai viện Quốc hội trong cuộc bầu cử tuần trước. Các ứng viên đảng Dn chủ cũng chiến thắng trong các cuộc bầu cử thống đốc ở nhiều bang, trong đó có Texas, nơi có nhiều trung tm dữ liệu. [...] Một số nhà đầu tư lo ngại những chiến thắng này có thể dẫn đến việc siết chặt quy định đối với AI và các trung tm dữ liệu.  
   
Mối lo này đã gy ra làn sóng bán tháo cổ phiếu bán dẫn và các cổ phiếu khác liên quan đến AI. Hôm thứ Năm, chỉ số Nasdaq gồm nhiều cổ phiếu công nghệ ở New York giảm hơn 5%. Cổ phiếu công nghệ đã phần nào khôi phục vào ngày hôm sau nhưng các nhà đầu tư vẫn thận trọng. [...] Một số chuyên gia cho rằng các công ty trung tm dữ liệu mới nổi có thể gặp khó khăn về vốn nếu các quy định chặt chẽ hơn làm chậm tiến độ các dự án xy dựng mới. Các công ty này đã dựa vào khoản vay để mở rộng kinh doanh.  
   
Nguồn tin thị trường cho biết điều đó có nghĩa là cổ phiếu công nghệ có thể vẫn bất ổn trong thời gian trước mắt.

items.title: Sam Altman
items.summary:
Here is a photo of my family. I love them more than anything.

![](https://phaven-prod.s3.amazonaws.com/files/image_part/asset/3439526/q4Xtf4iMYA_SCrMc8hMfnF_k3UE/medium_WhatsApp_Image_2026-02-28_at_15.26.14__4_.jpeg)

Images have power, I hope. Normally we try to be pretty private, but in this case I am sharing a photo in the hopes that it might dissuade the next person from throwing a Molotov cocktail at our house, no matter what they think about me.

The first person did it last night, at 3:45 am in the morning. Thankfully it bounced off the house and no one got hurt.

Words have power too. There was an incendiary article about me a few days ago. Someone said to me yesterday they thought it was coming at a time of great anxiety about AI and that it made things more dangerous for me. I brushed it aside.

Now I am awake in the middle of the night and pissed, and thinking that I have underestimated the power of words and narratives. This seems like as good of a time as any to address a few things.

**First**, what I believe.

\*Working towards prosperity for everyone, empowering all people, and advancing science and technology are moral obligations for me.

\*AI will be the most powerful tool for expanding human capability and potential that anyone has ever seen. Demand for this tool will be essentially uncapped, and people will do incredible things with it. The world deserves huge amounts of AI and we must figure out how to make it happen.

\*It will not all go well. The fear and anxiety about AI is justified; we are in the process of witnessing the largest change to society in a long time, and perhaps ever. We have to get safety right, which is not just about aligning a model—we urgently need a society-wide response to be resilient to new threats. This includes things like new policy to help navigate through a difficult economic transition in order to get to a much better future.

\*AI has to be democratized; power cannot be too concentrated. Control of the future belongs to all people and their institutions. AI needs to empower people individually, and we need to make decisions about our future and the new rules collectively. I do not think it is right that a few AI labs would make the most consequential decisions about the shape of our future.

\*Adaptability is critical. We are all learning about something new very quickly; some of our beliefs will be right and some will be wrong, and sometimes we will need to change our mind quickly as the technology develops and society evolves. No one understands the impacts of superintelligence yet, but they will be immense.

**Second**, some personal reflections.

As I reflect on my own work in the first decade of OpenAI, I can point to a lot of things I’m proud of and a bunch of mistakes.

I was thinking about our upcoming trial with Elon and remembering how much I held the line on not being willing to agree to the unilateral control he wanted over OpenAI. I’m proud of that, and the narrow path we navigated then to allow the continued existence of OpenAI, and all the achievements that followed.

I am not proud of being conflict-averse, which has caused great pain for me and OpenAI. I am not proud of handling myself badly in a conflict with our previous board that led to a huge mess for the company. I have made many other mistakes throughout the insane trajectory of OpenAI; I am a flawed person in the center of an exceptionally complex situation, trying to get a little better each year, always working for the mission. We knew going into this how huge the stakes of AI were, and that the personal disagreements between well-meaning people I cared about would be amplified greatly. But it’s another thing to live through these bitter conflicts and often to have to arbitrate them, and the costs have been serious. I am sorry to people I’ve hurt and wish I had learned more faster.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. items.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation, source says | Reuters
items.summary:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI has closed ‌on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round ​that values the company ​at $1.25 trillion, a source familiar with ⁠the matter said on Friday.

The $11 ​billion raised so far represents ​only a portion of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, while ​the company's valuation has ​come down from the $1.5 trillion level it ‌had ⁠initially sought, two investors said. items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections. [...] OpenAI depends on data centers to train its AI models and serve customers, and Friar said she doesn't think the midterms dramatically changed anything for the company.

"If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we're going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them," Friar said. [...] "When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how do we keep investing to meet that customer demand," Friar told CNBC's Sara Eisen in an interview at the Citi TMT Leadership Summit at California's Pebble Beach. "It starts early with having built relationships with all of the hyperscalers, and it will continue to mean that we raise capital."
